trial.protocol: Both runs were driven to the same finish line: implement, run the shared gate, feed any failure back verbatim, repeat until the gate is green. A run is finished only when all 11 gate tests pass.
trial.why_this_supersedes_trial_1: Trial 1 stopped each run at the point where the agent declared itself done. Run A declared done while still failing 3 of 11 gate tests, so its 72 s was never a time to completion. Measuring a run where it claims success, rather than where it passes acceptance, flatters whichever run gives up earliest. Trial 1 is kept in scoreboard-trial1.json for comparison.
trial.harness: Copilot CLI sub-agent, identical for both runs. NOT VS Code Copilot.
trial.run_order: A first (21:16:38Z), then B (21:18:58Z), sequentially. Never in parallel, to keep CPU contention out of the elapsed times.
trial.cache: Cold for both: fresh workspaces rebuilt from the same baseline, fresh agent, no prior context.
trial.prompt: Byte-identical for both runs except the workspace path. Templates in demo/prompts/. Neither run was ever shown the gate source.
trial.discarded: One earlier Run A attempt (agent c20c46cf) was discarded and its workspace rebuilt, because a typo in the prompt broke the byte-identical control. It is excluded from every figure here.

held_constant: Same baseline, copied into two separate workspaces
Same model, same harness, same machine
Same failure-feedback protocol and the same feedback wording
Same 11-test gate, executed by the operator, hidden from both runs
difference: Run B's workspace carries preparation: an AGENTS.md brief stating the overdue rule and the repo constraints, a curated 100-case fixture, and an npm run test:fast command that targets it. The preparation does not implement the feature.

A.label: Harness as-is
A.inner_loop_command: npm test (seeds 400,000 rows, ~1.36 s per run)
turn_1_failures: overdue filter returns only unpaid invoices past the as-of date
overdue combines with the existing status filter
pagination stays at 25 rows per page
A.root_cause: Turn 1 implemented overdue as status === 'SENT' && dueDate < asOf, which silently drops past-due DRAFT invoices. The feature request never defined which statuses still count as owed, so the agent guessed, plausibly and wrongly. All three failures trace to that one line. Turn 2 corrected it after being shown the gate output.

B.label: Harness prepared, brief and fixture
B.inner_loop_command: npm run test:fast (100 curated rows, ~0.22 s per run)
B.root_cause: Implemented overdue as status !== 'PAID' && status !== 'CANCELLED' && dueDate < asOf, matching the rule stated in AGENTS.md. No guess was required.

ratios_to_the_same_gate.wall_clock: A 131 s vs B 72 s, A cost 1.8x

how_ai_usage_was_measured.source: Local session store table assistant_usage_events, filtered by the agent_id of each run.
how_ai_usage_was_measured.fields: input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, reasoning_tokens, total_nano_aiu, duration_ms
how_ai_usage_was_measured.unit: AI units (AIU) = total_nano_aiu / 1e9. This is the billing unit, not a token count.
how_ai_usage_was_measured.query: SELECT agent_id, COUNT(*), SUM(input_tokens), SUM(output_tokens), SUM(cache_read_tokens), SUM(total_nano_aiu)/1e9 FROM assistant_usage_events WHERE agent_id IN (...) GROUP BY agent_id
how_ai_usage_was_measured.note: The cloud session_usage view lags by days and returned nothing for this trial. The local table is written in real time and does record sub-agent usage against agent_id, which is why trial 1 wrongly reported usage as unavailable.

measured_inner_loop.caveat: A faster inner loop is not a token saving and not a scale test. 100 rows says nothing about behaviour at 400,000.

honest_reading: Driven to the same gate, the prepared run cost less on every axis measured: one turn instead of two, 72 s instead of 131 s, and 13.6 AI units instead of 22.1. The interesting part is why. Run A was not slower because its tests were slower. It was slower because it had to guess what overdue meant, guessed wrong, and needed a round trip through the gate to find out. The brief did not make the model faster. It removed an ambiguity the model could not resolve from the code.
still_not_measured: Run B's preparation cost. It was authored before the trial and was not timed, so it is not inside B's 72 s and no fair end-to-end total can be computed from this trial. The preparation is reusable across every later change, but that is an argument, not a measurement.
